findings.desc: quality: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:512-537 enforceConvergenceBreakerGate declares opts.store as a narrow Pick<StoryStore, readStory|readReviewRuns|readReviewPasses|storyDirPath>, then at line 537 calls collectBreakerCounters(opts.store as StoryStore, ...) with an unnecessary/unsafe cast back to the full StoryStore class. This defeats the point of the narrower Pick: if collectBreakerCounters later calls another StoryStore method not present in the Pick, TypeScript will not catch the mismatch (the cast hides it) and the failure only surfaces at runtime. Fix: give collectBreakerCounters the same narrow Pick type (or a shared exported alias) so the cast can be removed. Note enforceConvergenceBreakerGate itself has zero direct test coverage in tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts (only the pure assessBreaker and standalone I/O helpers are exercised there), so this cast is unverified by the new smoke.

quality: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:1222,1241,1305 the new convergence-breaker call sites extract the target storyId via the raw cast (parsed.storyId as string) || activeStory?.storyId instead of reusing storyIdFromArgs, which is already imported into this exact file (see line 52/882/1074/1114) and is used by enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate (packages/main/src/cli/ownership-gate.ts:242) at the same choke point one line above. storyIdFromArgs is type-safe (typeof-narrows args.storyId, no unchecked cast) and also resolves the --story alias and the autopilot-run-id fallback; the new inline cast does neither. Net effect: a command that supplies the story via --story (accepted by the owner-lease gate) silently resolves to no storyId for the breaker gate/gate-failure counters, so enforceConvergenceBreakerGate no-ops (storyId is falsy, early return at convergence-breaker.ts:520) and the reset/bump blocks skip their sid branch too -- an inconsistency between the two gates that share the same choke point, and an unsafe cast where a safe, already-imported helper does the same job correctly.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:267-286 + handlers/story.ts:57-60 + core/story-owner-lease.ts:824-831: the one-shot auto-recovery/human-ack-resume only re-baselines the ADVANCE signal (advanceBaseline=advanceCount); it never resets/windows takeoverCount (takeover-count.json is write-only-increment for the entire story lifetime, bumped at story-owner-lease.ts:831, never decremented or reset by resumeBreakerState in convergence-breaker.ts:301-312 nor by story_resume in handlers/story.ts:58-60) and never windows the pass-rate ratio. Concrete false-freeze sequence for a story that legitimately accumulates >5 lease takeovers over its life (plausible for any multi-session/multi-day story, e.g. crash/session-handoff recoveries): (1) 6th takeover trips the breaker via takeover-signal on the next story_advance -> assessBreaker returns action=auto-recover (budget 0<1), state persisted with autoRecoveriesSpent=1, advance proceeds. (2) The VERY NEXT story_advance call re-reads takeoverCount, still =6>5 (nothing decremented it), re-trips, autoRecoveriesSpent(1) is no longer <AUTO_RECOVERY_BUDGET(1) -> action=freeze -> throws, hard-blocking the story even though it may now be perfectly healthy/converging. (3) A human runs story_resume --ack; resumeBreakerState resets autoRecoveriesSpent=0/frozen=false but leaves takeover-count.json untouched at 6. (4) The next story_advance re-trips via the SAME takeover signal, again auto-recovers (spends the fresh budget), and the call after that freezes again. The story is now PERMANENTLY stuck alternating one advance succeeds, next one freezes forever, requiring a human story_resume roughly every other story_advance for the rest of the story lifetime, with no way to genuinely clear it short of manually deleting the gitignored/undocumented takeover-count.json file on disk. This directly violates the CHK-002 userSees promise (After a first trip ... the story still advances) and the module header contract (auto-recovers ONCE so healthy autonomous work is unaffected) for any story whose takeover count ever crosses the threshold, and is a genuine false-freeze of a healthy story at the story_advance choke point. Pass-rate has the same structural gap (no windowing/baseline) but is a ratio so it can self-heal with enough future passes; takeover is an absolute non-decreasing count so it structurally never heals. The smoke test (tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts section 3) only covers the advance-count recovery path by hand-constructing a fixture where advanceCount stalls, never a re-assessment that reuses an unchanged elevated takeoverCount/passRate after auto-recovery or after story_resume, so this gap is untested. Fix: either window/re-baseline takeoverCount (and the pass-rate sample) the same way advanceCount is re-baselined on auto-recovery/resume, or have story_resume snapshot-baseline takeoverCount (a takeoverBaseline field) so only NEW takeovers after the ack can re-trip.
